design.const_series: all samples = 1 (zero patch after revin, sigma=0)
design.captured_state: last patch token of the 1280-dim residual stream
design.ridge: trace-scaled ridge lambda*trace(X^T X)/d, push-through dual form, features standardised on the training fold; K-fold pooled R^2 over phases, lambda grid [0.0003, 0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0]; nested variant selects lambda by inner 3-fold CV; null = fixed phase permutation of z(y)
design.gradient: autograd d/dx sum ||yhat-y||^2 through a differentiable reproduction of the decode prefill (TimesFM.decode itself runs under no_grad)
design.response: central finite differences, step eps=0.01, perturbation eps*cos(2 pi b t/32); M[f,b] = z_f(dyhat/ds); reported at a 32-sample and a 128-sample (full output patch) readout
design.caveats: z(y) is a pure phase family here (all tones unit power), so a linear probe of ANY smooth representation of the phase reads R^2~1; the R^2-vs-layer curve therefore detects total destruction of the tone, not a band-selective amplitude loss. The response matrix is the residual-free causal measure.

4.note: ||g|| is dominated by the residual ||yhat-y||, so it is large exactly on the destroyed bands; cos(g,x) and the shares are scale-free

response.note: rows = probed output band, cols = perturbed input band; M[f,b] = z_f(dyhat/ds) with s = amplitude of the eps*cos(2 pi b t/32) direction (1.0 = output tracks the input band). Central finite differences. The 32-sample readout cannot resolve 5.0 from 5.3 (0.3 cycle leak); the 128-sample readout can.

tokenizer_geometry.note: single phase-0 patch, raw tone + zero mask (same convention as probe.ring_probe); the constant series normalizes to the all-zero patch
